title: Determining the metabolic impact of postbiotics in mice
author: Anhê, Bhatwa, et al.

steps.title: Acclimatize and group mice
steps.instruction: Acclimatize mice for 1–2 weeks after arrival; use 12–25‑week‑old C57Bl6N or C57Bl6J mice, matched for weight (≈30 g), age, sex, strain, diet, and housing conditions (12 h light/dark, ad libitum food and water, consistent room temperature, same number per cage). Test 10–12 mice per treatment group as the minimum sample size.

steps.title: Prepare postbiotic stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve LPS and PGN (including DAP‑PGN, MDP‑PGN, FK565) in endotoxin‑free water to a concentration of 1 mg/mL; aliquot into 0.5–1.0 mL portions in MAXYMum Recovery® tubes (or similar) to minimise freeze‑thaw cycles; vortex each aliquot vigorously for at least 15 min using a ThermoMixer C® or comparable benchtop shaker; store aliquots at –20 °C. For injections, plan ~0.5 mL of LPS or FK565 stock per 30 mice (~30 g each) and ~3.0 mL of MDP stock per 30 mice.

steps.title: Standardize blood glucose measurement
steps.instruction: Use the same brand and model of glucometer and the same batch of glucose test strips for all measurements within and across experiments to avoid discrepancies in absolute blood glucose readings.

steps.title: Set up data analysis software
steps.instruction: Install GraphPad Prism version 8 or 9 (or equivalent) for graphical visualization, AUC calculation, and statistical analysis.

steps.title: Analyze glucose tolerance data
steps.instruction: Plot glucose excursion curves as XY graphs (Y = blood glucose in mmol/L, X = time in minutes). Calculate area under the curve (AUC) with baseline set to 0 for all curves. Test data distribution for normality using Shapiro‑Wilk, Kolmogorov‑Smirnov, Anderson‑Darling, or D’Agostino & Pearson tests (available in Prism 9). Choose statistical tests based on distribution: for two‑factor comparisons (e.g., PGN × LPS) use two‑way ANOVA with Tukey’s post‑test (p < 0.05 considered significant); if non‑parametric two‑way analysis is needed, use Kruskal‑Wallis on ranks or log‑transform data and retest normality before parametric ANOVA. For single‑factor comparisons (e.g., PGN vs saline) use unpaired Student’s t‑test (parametric) or Mann‑Whitney test (non‑parametric). Optionally, perform two‑way repeated‑measures ANOVA to assess glucose differences at individual time points, but prioritize AUC as the primary endpoint.

steps.title: Estimate protocol timeline
steps.instruction: Allocate 1–2 weeks for animal acclimatization and preparation before beginning injections and glucose tolerance testing.

description: Timing: 1–2 weeks We present a protocol for testing the impact of postbiotics on host metabolism in vivo, where examples are peptidoglycan (PGN) working in synergy or promoting tolerance when combined with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to alter blood glucose control. Our exemplar approach used meso-diaminopimelic acid (DAP)-PGN or muramyl dipeptide (MDP)-PGN and hexa-acylated LPS from Escherichia coli. This protocol allows testing the metabolic impact of postbiotics using a simple and efficient technique. This method also models the synergy or tolerance that can occur between postbiotics, which can provide insight into the interaction of microbial-derived molecules on host metabolic regulation. This protocol can be easily adapted to different types of PGN and/or LPS in addition to other postbiotics. However, adaptations using other postbiotics may require optimization, especially regarding the dose and timing of administration. Likewise, while this protocol describes the assessment of blood glucose control by means of a glucose tolerance test (GTT) following PGN and LPS administration, the main metabolic endpoint may also be adapted. Metabolic tests other than a GTT (i.e., insulin, pyruvate or lipid tolerance test) may require fasting strategies different from the one described herein. Animals: Ensure that all animal procedures were institutionally approved and comply with local ethics board guidelines. Mice procured from a vendor should be acclimatized for at least 1–2 weeks prior to testing. Different treatment groups must be matched for weight and age. Sex, strain, diet, room temperature, housing room, and number of mice per cage must be consistent across treatment groups and cohorts. Mice must be in a 12h light/dark cycle and have access to food and water ad libitum. The present protocol was optimized for 12–25-week-old C57Bl6N or C57Bl6J mice.
